document.heading: Changes to Chapter 3.02 - Hunting of Deer

citations.citation: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Res. No. 09-02-26-09

recital.text: the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Tribe of Chippewa Indians is a federally recognized Indian Tribe with a Constitution enacted pursuant to the Indian Reorganization Act of 1934, 25 U.S.C. Section 476; and
Article VI Section 1(n) of the Constitution directs the Tribal Council to encourage and foster the arts, crafts, traditions, culture, wildlife, and natural resources of the Band; and
that the Tribal Council hereby approves the following changes to Chapter 3.02 - Hunting of Deer:

para.text: In Chapter 3.02 change the word deer to the words big game; and
In Section 3.02.020 add the definition:
Big Game: deer, bear, and elk

procedural-data.text: I, the undersigned, as Secretary of the Bad River Band of Lake Superior Chippewa Indians of Wisconsin, hereby certify that the Tribal Council is composed of 7 members, of whom 7, constituting a quorum, were present at a meeting duly called, noticed, and held on the 2 day of September, 2026, that the foregoing resolution was duly adopted at such meeting by a vote of 6 for, 0 against, and 0 abstaining.

codify:replace.codified:doc: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal Code

section.heading: Findings
section.text: The Tribal Council finds that the lands now comprising the Bad River Reservation were traditional hunting grounds for the ancestors of the Tribe; that these lands were selected as a Reservation because of their wealth of fish, game, and wild rice; that deer and bear have been a nutritional staple for members of the Tribe for generations beyond memory; that deer continue to provide a substantial portion of the protein and other nutritional needs of the Tribe's members; that high unemployment and cash-poor local economy indicate that deer will remain critical as a food source for the Tribe's members; that pressure on the deer population by non-member sport hunting reduces the availability of deer as a food source for members; that non-members flaunting of tribal conservation laws has contributed to a decline in the reservation deer population; and that effective regulation of both member and non-member hunting of big game is essential for the preservation of the species in numbers sufficient to supply the economic and nutritional needs of the Tribe's members.

codify:replace.codified:doc: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal Code

para.text: "Conservation Department" means the Conservation Department of the Tribe.
"Member" means any person who is enrolled or is eligible for enrollment in the Tribe, or who is recognized as a member of the Tribe by the Tribal Council.
"Non-members" means any person who does not come within the definition of member.
"Reservation" means the Bad River Reservation.
"Tribal Council" means the Tribal Council of the Tribe.
"Tribe" means the Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Tribe of Chippewa Indians of the Bad River Reservation.
Big Game: deer, bear

codify:replace.codified:doc: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal Code

para.text: No person shall hunt or take any big game within the reservation except during the open season.
No person shall hunt or take any big game within the reservation in excess of the limit allowed.

codify:replace.codified:doc: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal Code

para.text: No member who takes a big game shall fail to comply with reporting of kill regulations as established by the Conservation Department.
No non-member who takes a big game shall fail to report the kill to the Conservation Department within 72 hours of the kill.

codify:replace.codified:doc: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal Code

para.text: No person shall, while hunting big game:
Hunt with any means other than the use of a gun discharged from the shoulder or a bow and arrow.
Have in possession while hunting any poisoned, drugged, or explosive tipped arrow.
Have in possession while hunting any incendiary type ammunition, except hunter distress flares.
Be in possession of handguns (any gun having a barrel less than 12 inches in length) if under the age of 18 years unless supervised by an adult 18 years of age or older.
Hunt with the aid of a dog.
Use arrows that are not well sharpened broad head blades. Broad head blades may not be less than seven-eights of an inch or more than one-half inches in width.
No person shall, while hunting big game:
Discharge a firearm on lands of another within 500 yards of a building devoted to human occupancy without permission of the owner or occupant.
Appropriate, molest, or disturb any big game or the carcass or part thereof which has been lawfully reduced to possession by another without having that person's consent.
Hunt with the use of an airplane, including the use of an airplane to spot, rally or drive big game for hunters on the ground.
Put out bait containing poison where it might cause the destruction of wild animals or birds or possess poison while hunting or trapping.
Place, operate, or attend, spread, or set any net, pitfall, spring gun, pivot gun, or any other contrivance for the purpose of catching or which catch or take big game.
Take or attempt to take any big game with the aid of any explosives.
Train dogs by pursuing big game.
Fail to make every reasonable effort to retrieve all big game crippled or killed.

codify:replace.codified:doc: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal Code

section.heading: Licensing
section.text: No person shall hunt or take big game who does not have in his or her possession a valid license issued to him or her by the Conservation Department, or who does not have or is not eligible to receive a membership or enrollment card of the Tribe.

codify:replace.codified:doc: Bad River Band of the Lake Superior Chippewa Indians Tribal Code

para.text: Any big game taken in violation of this chapter may be seized by the Conservation Department and may be ordered forfeited.
Any equipment used in the violation of this chapter maybe seized by the Conservation Department and ordered forfeited.
